key_insight: Transient ion current (TIC/BACE) in perovskite solar cells is often limited by transport-layer capacitance rather than by the perovskite’s true ionic density.
engineering_relevance: Accurate ion quantification requires accounting for transport-layer properties, otherwise TIC can overestimate ionic parameters by orders of magnitude.
method: Varied C60 electron-transport-layer thickness in p-i-n devices.
Varied Spiro-OMeTAD hole-transport-layer doping in n-i-p devices.
Used drift-diffusion simulations and TL-thickness extrapolation to infer absorber ionic properties.
evidence_signal: Experiments across two device architectures confirmed that the TIC signal scales strongly with transport-layer properties and that extrapolating toward a transport-layer-free limit recovers intrinsic ionic conductivity.
watch_item: TIC-based ion density can be inflated by transport-layer capacitance and possibly by trapped-carrier release, so raw measurements should not be interpreted as absorber ion density without correction.
paper_title: Overcoming Transport Layer Bottlenecks to Quantify Ionic Parameters from Transient Ion Current Measurements of Perovskite Solar Cells
